what: Sharing the native test-process runner exposed eight intentional stop sites in the ordinary child_case helper of signals_tests.rs. The old duplicate runner had six counted stops, so the launcher row rose from 219 to 221 even though the complete 137-test launcher run passed.
cost: The current gate reports a launcher stop increase inside the broader failed stops row; raising its ceiling would preserve a source-classification error.
cause: The classifier recognizes the module's cfg(all(test, not(blaze_check))) and pub(crate) visibility but drops its path attribute. The walker searches signals/tests.rs instead of the declared signals_tests.rs. The former child function's own test attribute masked the missing file-level classification until it became a shared helper.
class: a source inventory follows logical module names without their explicit source paths
prevention: Carry the literal path attached to the module declaration through shared source classification. Follow test-only reach to the actual file while keeping files and descendants also reachable from production counted. A source exclusion needs a certain declaration or a whole-file test cfg; unknown module-directory ownership never supplies that proof. Preserve production roots declared by Cargo, including a physical source used as both a root and an ordinary module.
workaround: None. Keep the signal and panic controls and existing policy ceilings; do not hide the helper behind an extra test-file exemption.
fix: The shared classifier carries typed module paths, reads attributes lexically outside strings and comments, and proves test-only files before revoking candidates reachable from production. Cargo roots use the existing TOML reader; fixture manifests retain the existing test-directory policy. The duplicate scanner consumes the same classifier. The first hosted run compiled the scripts but found a flawed selftest oracle: an orphan signals/tests.rs was expected to count despite the existing test-file naming convention. The corrected fixture gives that file an explicit production parent; later default-path controls use checks.rs and remove only its cfg to prove the cause. The measured two new allocator-fixing signatures are removed by reusing the existing lossy text reader and accepting directory views instead of a concrete owned manifest cache. Independent review confirms that the additional file-items and ladder sites are unchanged helpers reached by unconditional production example imports: they remain counted as real debt. Unsupported module contexts remain conservative, no policy ceiling is raised, and the next hosted run passed the full scanner selftest suite. Its canonical inventory confirms blaze-script signatures remain 117. Only measured downward allocation/untyped rows are adopted; the production-example debt remains held to its existing ceilings.
